name.description: scenario identity; defaults to the filename (sans extension) if omitted — an explicit value overrides that and keys the run dir + cassette

baseline.description: platform baseline to run against (auto-synced via `cowork-harness sync`)

session.description: hand-authored session setup file (pre-prompt: model, mounts, discovery); defaults to an all-defaults inline session

fidelity.description: isolation tier (REQUIRED): protocol (L0, no sandbox) | container/microvm (force a VM-loop tier) | hostloop (force host-loop) | cowork (auto-pick host-loop vs. container via Cowork's own gate logic). `container` models the VM loop, while Cowork's local lane runs the host loop by default (gate 1143815894) — a bare relative path lands elsewhere, the shell starts elsewhere, and the offered tool set differs. Name hostloop to match that lane, cowork to auto-pick the way Cowork does, or container to model the VM loop deliberately.

execution.description: local only (the default): a multi-leg scenario runs locally

lane.description: local only (the default): a multi-leg scenario runs on the local lane; lane: remote is refused

workdir.description: persistent (default): every leg runs in the same session tree, so a leg sees earlier legs' files at the same paths — a persistent workspace, not Cowork. cowork-task: each prompt leg gets a new session root; connected folders carry over, outputs do not (a model of a new local Cowork task, unverified)

id.description: the leg's id, unique within the scenario: 1-64 of [a-z0-9_-], starting with a letter or digit. It names the leg's run dir (legs/<id>) and is what --leg <id> takes

prompt.description: the user turn of this leg's fresh agent session

host_action.description: a command run in the leg runtime; no agent, no tokens

status.description: a status file read before the action; its string fields fill `{status.<field>}` in `run`

artifact.description: a JSON status file to read before the action, relative to the work root as assertion paths are (`outputs/…`)

expect.description: top-level fields the status file must have: `{field: {not_null: true}}` requires a non-null value; any other value must equal the field's (compared as serialized JSON, so object key order counts)

run.description: argv, one element per argument; `{status.<field>}` is substituted per element. Never a shell string

session.description: this leg's overlay on the scenario session

timeout_ms.description: this prompt leg's wall-clock budget for its agent run, in ms; on expiry the harness kills the agent and the leg ends result:error / errorSource:timeout. Omitted = no timeout. Refused on a host_action leg, whose limit is host_action.timeout (seconds)

legs.description: the legs, run in order, each a fresh agent session (prompt) or a host command (host_action): the first is a prompt leg, at least two are, and a leg after one that failed is skipped

answers.description: scripted answers, matched in order: AskUserQuestion gates by question-text regex, tool-permission gates by tool name (`when_tool`)

on_unanswered.description: policy when a gate arrives with no matching `answers:` rule — `fail` (default for `run`, deterministic) | `first` (pick the first offered option) | `llm` (delegate to a decider LLM) | `prompt` (interactive; valid only via `skill --on-unanswered prompt` or the adaptive-TTY default — rejected in scenario YAML under `run`)

expect_denied.description: hosts whose egress must have been DENIED: graded once for the scenario, over every leg's egress and every host action's, when every leg ran

skills.description: named `skills/<name>` dirs this scenario exercises, scoping the cassette-staleness hash to just those (+ shared plugin roots); omitted/empty hashes the whole mounted tree

requires_capabilities.description: capability families (e.g. office_convert, ocr, pdf_tables) this scenario's core path needs; the run hard-fails if the tier omits or can't verify one, unless `allow_missing_capability: true` is set on the relevant assertion

allow_host_hooks.description: required consent for `fidelity: protocol` when a staged plugin declares runnable hooks (`<plugin>/hooks/hooks.json`) — the CLI runs them as native host processes under your account with no container sandbox; plugins without hooks need no opt-in

workspace_fixture.description: a directory (relative to the scenario file) whose contents are copied into the session's outputs/ before the first leg; a later leg starts from the previous leg's end state. The same rules as a single scenario's workspace_fixture

description: cowork-harness MULTI-LEG scenario YAML — `legs:` in place of `prompt:`: each leg a prompt (a fresh agent session) or a host_action (argv run in the leg runtime). STRUCTURAL validation only: a leg's `assert:` is checked by the loader (a prompt leg takes the ordinary assertion keys, a host_action leg files only plus exit_code / stdout_matches / stdout_not_matches), as are the cross-leg rules (the first leg is a prompt leg, at least two prompt legs, unique ids). Run `cowork-harness lint <file>` and `cowork-harness record <file> --dry-run`. See docs/scenario.md, "Multi-leg scenarios".
